note: Ids are project-namespaced, not Freebase MIDs. Descriptions checked against citation_uri on 2026-11-19.

entries.name: erhu
entries.description: Sounds of a two-stringed Chinese bowed fiddle with a small resonator covered in python skin, held upright, with the bow hair passing between the strings.

scope.excludes: other huqin: jinghu, gaohu, zhonghu, banhu; "huqin" without erhu

entries.name: pipa
entries.description: Sounds of a four-stringed Chinese plucked lute with a pear-shaped body and frets, held upright.

scope.accepted_names: pipa lute, chinese pipa, 琵琶
scope.excludes: other Chinese lutes (liuqin, ruan, yueqin, sanxian); Japanese biwa

entries.name: dizi
entries.description: Sounds of a Chinese transverse flute, usually of bamboo, often fitted with a thin membrane over an extra hole that gives a buzzing timbre.

scope.accepted_names: dizi flute, chinese bamboo flute, 笛子
scope.excludes: end-blown xiao; free-reed bawu and hulusi; Western concert flute

entries.name: guzheng
entries.description: Sounds of a Chinese plucked zither with many strings over movable bridges.

scope.excludes: guqin (no bridges); Japanese koto; Korean gayageum; Vietnamese dan tranh

entries.name: charango
entries.description: Sounds of a small Andean plucked instrument of the lute family with five courses of paired strings.

scope.excludes: ukulele, cuatro, mandolin and other non-Andean small lutes (proposed 2026-11-19, unconfirmed)

entries.name: quena
entries.description: Sounds of an Andean end-blown flute with a notch cut into the end, traditionally of cane or wood, with finger holes.

scope.excludes: quenacho (larger, lower); pinkillo and other duct flutes; ney

entries.name: siku (zampoña)
entries.description: Sounds of an Andean panpipe (zampona) of bamboo or cane pipes, split across two rows played in alternation.

scope.accepted_names: siku, zampoña, zampona, antara panpipe, andean panpipe
scope.excludes: non-Andean panpipes (Romanian nai, Western pan flute); ensembles of more than one player are solo = n

entries.name: bombo legüero
entries.description: Sounds of the bombo leguero, a double-headed Argentine folk drum traditionally made of a hollowed tree trunk with animal-skin heads, struck on the head and the wooden rim.

scope.accepted_names: bombo legüero, bombo leguero, bombo andino
scope.excludes: Western bass drum, kick drums, synthesized drums, maracatu and other non-Andean bombos

entries.name: oud
entries.description: Sounds of a short-necked, fretless, pear-shaped lute played with a plectrum, in Arab, Turkish and Persian music.

scope.excludes: European lute; baglama/saz and other long-necked lutes; cumbus

entries.name: ney
entries.description: Sounds of an end-blown flute made of cane or giant reed, used in Arab, Turkish and Persian music.

scope.accepted_names: ney flute, nay flute, ney turkish, ney arabic

entries.name: qanun
entries.description: Sounds of a large trapezoidal box zither of Arab and Turkish music, plucked, with many courses of strings and small levers (mandals) that change a course's pitch during playing.

scope.excludes: santur, cimbalom and other hammered zithers; guzheng and other East Asian zithers; harp

entries.name: darbuka
entries.description: Sounds of a single-headed goblet drum played with the fingertips and palms.

scope.accepted_names: darbuka, darbouka, doumbek, dumbek, goblet drum, derbake
scope.excludes: Persian tombak; frame drums (riq, daf, bendir); djembe (proposed 2026-11-19, unconfirmed)
